title: Use forward slashes for git paths, never path.join()
context: path.join() produces backslash-separated paths on Windows (e.g., `.github\x`). These keys are written to .gitattributes and passed to git as pathspecs, both of which are always POSIX-style. On Windows, the backslash string never matches the forward-slash allowlist in hunchAttributesAreSafe, causing .gitattributes validation to fail deterministically. Four prior fix attempts failed because they didn't address the content mismatch at the source. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.); con_8460b6770f (Config/provider writers must merge idempotently into existing user files and refuse to clobber an unparseable file).
decision: Replace path.join() calls in GROUNDING_WRITERS and WHOLLY_OWNED_GROUNDING with hardcoded forward-slash strings (e.g., `".github/copilot-instructions.md"`). Git paths and config keys are platform-invariant; they must use POSIX-style separators, not OS-dependent path construction.
consequences: Windows builds will pass .gitattributes safety validation
Git pathspec operations work identically on all platforms
Config keys now platform-invariant, matching the allowlist they're validated against
WHOLLY_OWNED_GROUNDING Set membership comparison works across platforms
alternatives_rejected: Normalize backslashes during comparison (git treats the literal string; normalization doesn't fix the actual path mismatch)
Use path.join() everywhere and normalize in consumers (maintains the bug, adds comparison complexity)
Conditional platform-specific logic (unnecessary; POSIX is the standard for git/config)
